items.title: 52220_Woody Herman oral history interview
items.q: their top two people were, to the best of my recollection, Frank Sinatra and Dinah Shore.

ctx.x: Very. And, of course, I was there during a period which was not a long one, where a guy -- Manny Sachs, who was Sinatra's man, and he liked music and he had a flare for putting good things together. And very few suggestions, other than, 'Can I do something for you?'

items.title: 52220_Woody Herman oral history interview
items.q: I don't think there are too many Frank Tiberians around.

ctx.x: Yeah. He brings a classical tone, without him that pavanne wouldn't sound the same.

Well, he's -- I don't think there are too many Frank Tiberians around. If he was a man of his kind, he would be now in Atlantic City, probably the subcontractor at the gaming place or something. But he's not a man of his time, he's a man who still has the spirit to be out here.
Yeah, it's amazing. Yeah. He's writing a book, I understand.
